subject.title: [Feature]: Compaction: configurable model override + flush-then-reset mode

question: Should OpenClaw add a compaction-threshold flush-then-reset policy now that compaction and memoryFlush model overrides are shipped, and what privacy/provider/session-state semantics should it use?
rationale: The remaining request changes config surface, silent model execution, durable memory writes, and session reset behavior; source inspection cannot decide the product and security policy safely.

options.title: Design unified reset-memory policy first
options.body: Keep this issue open and align the compaction-threshold reset mode with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/45608 so explicit, daily, idle, and compaction-pressure resets share one bounded policy.

options.title: Add default-off resetAfterFlush
options.body: Approve a narrow default-off `memoryFlush.resetAfterFlush` mode with explicit provider, timeout, notification, and regression proof requirements.

options.title: Reject automatic reset-after-flush
options.body: Keep compaction as the canonical context-preservation path and rely on model overrides, memory flush, and manual reset flows for cost control.

recommendation.title: Design unified reset-memory policy first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and align the compaction-threshold reset mode with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/45608 so explicit, daily, idle, and compaction-pressure resets share one bounded policy.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is tied to the original memory-flush behavior and current reset-adjacent runtime code, making him the best available owner for the product/security choice.
